answer: Bounded reputation leverage: a grader's signal weight equals own stake plus borrowed stake, but each loan pays per-epoch interest and leverage is capped relative to the kernel of earned reputation. Like copper carrying only so much current, one locked collateral backs a single borrower, bound to both keys. A lender whose borrower is judged collusive is slashed alongside, so circular lending among sybil accounts collapses into one slashable cluster. A farm cannot amplify N empty accounts without N real collaterals plus interest; honest graders borrow cheaply against proven history.
